articles.title: Tonal upgrades its smart weightlifting machine with heavier weights and a better camera
articles.summary: Tonal has launched the Tonal 2. The updated smart home trainer lets users lift up to 250 pounds of weight, comes with an improved camera, and more.
articles.body: Tonal on Wednesday launched the Tonal 2, an upgraded version of its smart in-home strength trainer. Launched in 2018, the Tonal is a wall-mounted strength training machine with electromagnetically adjustable resistance and a touchscreen display. It can monitor lifting form, offer virtual coaching, predict and set the optimal weight for each exercise, and responsively adjust as you lift for a personalized workout. The company also offers on-demand workouts. Along with sporting a new all-black design and chrome accents, the Tonal 2 comes with a host of meaningful internal improvements, including a new adaptive weight system with up to 250 pounds of digital resistance, up from the 200 pounds in the original trainer. The latest version of the trainer now offers drop sets via a software update also available on the Tonal 1, with the option to automatically reduce weight during a set as muscle fatigue builds up. The Tonal 2 also comes with a new “Aero HIIT” mode, which lets you combine cardio and strength training into a single session. Tonal also improved its optional Smart View feature, which uses cameras to watch your form and give real-time coaching cues. On the Tonal 1, Smart View required you to use your phone camera, and used the on-device camera for a second angle in some exercises; on the Tonal 2, it uses the built-in camera, with an option to use your smartphone for a second angle. The company says the camera also can now use AI to “analyze 500 data points per second.” The Tonal 2 is available now, starting at $4,295, not including delivery and installation, plus a $495 “smart accessories bundle” that the company’s website says is “required to unlock the best Tonal experience.” It also requires a $60/month subscription, with a one-year commitment to start. Tonal noted on Instagram it will be introducing a trade-in program for existing Tonal 1 owners looking to upgrade, but didn’t give specifics. Tonal told The Verge the Tonal 2 can be mounted on the original Tonal’s existing wall mount for easier installation.

articles.title: Bigg Boss Kannada 13: Wild card entrant Kumari gets evicted after a short stint in the house
articles.summary: Bigg Boss Kannada Season 13 witnessed another eviction during the weekend episode, with wild card entrant Kumari bidding goodbye to the house.
articles.body: Bigg Boss Kannada Season 13 witnessed another eviction during the weekend episode, with wild card entrant Kumari bidding goodbye to the house. Having entered the reality show just a few weeks ago, Kumari's journey came to an end within a short span of almost three weeks, leaving her fellow contestants emotional.This week's elimination process saw seven contestants nominated for eviction: Asiya, Dhanush, Gagan, Jagadeesh, Kiran, Kumari and Prashant. After the elimination proceedings, Kumari was announced as the contestant leaving the house.During her eviction, Kumari got emotional and admitted that she could not live up to the expectations viewers had of her. She acknowledged that she might not have delivered the kind of performance the audience anticipated, making her exit an emotional one.From Agnipareekshe to the Bigg Boss house: Kumari's journeyKumari's journey on Bigg Boss Kannada 13 was particularly special, as she was not a regular celebrity contestant but someone who had already caught the audience's attention through the reality show Agnipareekshe.A 20-year-old from Nanjangud, Kumari made a mark on Agnipareekshe with her straightforward nature and unfiltered way of expressing herself. She reportedly became the first contestant on the platform to receive the green signal from all four judges, making her a popular face among viewers even before entering the Bigg Boss house.Although she did not make it to the final stage of Agnipareekshe, fate had another opportunity waiting for her. Following the exit of Sangeetha Bhat and Modern Mahakavi Manja from Bigg Boss Kannada 13, Kumari was given a second chance to showcase her personality and talent as a wild card entrant.She entered the Bigg Boss house alongside fellow Agnipareekshe contestant Lakshmi during the festive Dasara period. From participating in the initial tasks to gradually finding her place among the housemates, Kumari began a new chapter in her reality television journey.A short journey that left an impressionDespite her relatively short stint, Kumari managed to build connections inside the house. Her innocent demeanour, candid conversations and straightforward approach made her a contestant who stood out in her own way.Her interactions with fellow housemates also brought out an endearing side of her personality. She gradually became part of the household dynamics, and her presence was acknowledged by contestants who shared a warm bond with her.However, the past week proved challenging for Kumari. She was reportedly dealing with health issues, which affected her participation in the tasks. Her limited involvement during this crucial phase may have also affected her journey in the competition.Her eviction was an emotional moment for the housemates, with several contestants visibly affected by her departure. For someone who had entered the show with hopes of making the most of her second opportunity, the journey ended sooner than expected.While Kumari admitted that she could not meet the audience's expectations, her Bigg Boss journey gave her an opportunity to reach a wider audience beyond Agnipareekshe. Though her stint was brief, she leaves the house with a memorable experience and the recognition of having made it to one of Kannada television's biggest reality shows.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. articles.title: Birdfy’s smart feeders now identify birds without a subscription.
articles.summary:
Starting today, new and existing owners of the company’s smart bird feeders will receive an unlimited number of identifications of over 6,000 different species when a bird lands to feed. Previously, free users were limited to only 10 AI bird recognitions per day. Those wanting more details, including a bird’s sex, age category, and health estimates, can opt for the $79.99-per-year Birdfy Membership Plus subscription or the $149.99-per-year Pro option.

articles.title: The 16GB Raspberry Pi 5 got another ‘unavoidable’ RAM price hike
articles.summary: The 16GB Raspberry Pi 5 got an $80 price hike, bringing it up to $385, due to ongoing shortages of RAM and other components.
articles.body: The Raspberry Pi 5 with 16GB of RAM now costs $385 after an $80 price hike, the latest in a string of increases driven by the ongoing RAM shortage. This configuration launched at $120 and now costs more than triple that price. The 16GB versions of the Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 also got a $40 price hike and now cost between $375 and $415. According to Raspberry Pi CEO Eben Upton, these price hikes were driven specifically by a lack of “alternative supply” for 16GB DRAM, on top of shortages for other components. Upton says, “Though these increases are unavoidable, we know they are unwelcome news for our customers. We encourage you to make sure you’re not paying for more memory than you need.” Upton suggested using Pis with less memory or older Pi models as alternatives to the pricey 16GB model. Unfortunately, other Raspberry Pi 5 configurations have also gotten more expensive — the 2GB version got a price hike last month. At $385, the 16GB Raspberry Pi 5 is nearing the price of a desktop mini PC. Upton reiterated the company’s plans to reverse the price hikes, saying, “the current memory landscape is difficult but ultimately temporary, and we look forward to rolling back our price increases when memory costs fall once again.”

articles.title: Ninja’s first-ever microwave just replaced two of my kitchen appliances at once | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The Ninja Crispi Microwave stands out for its FusionCrisp technology, which combines the speed of a microwave with the crispy results you'd expect from an air fryer.
articles.body:
I never thought I’d get excited about replacing my microwave, but the Ninja Crispi Microwave and Air Fryer has made a pretty convincing case for ditching two appliances and making room for one. Combining a microwave with a built-in air fryer, it’s designed to speed up everyday cooking, give leftovers their crunch back and, perhaps best of all, free up some valuable kitchen counter space.

Priced at $449.99, it’s certainly not a budget-friendly microwave. But this is no ordinary machine for heating leftover soup. Ninja has paired a 1,000W microwave with a 1,700W air fryer system, powered by its FusionCrisp technology, which combines the speed of microwave cooking with the golden, crispy results you’d typically expect from an air fryer.

Think leftover pizza, chicken tenders, fries, and all those foods that tend to turn sad and soggy in a traditional microwave. Instead, the idea is to get food that’s piping hot and juicy on the inside, with a deliciously crisp, golden finish on the outside. In other words, no more choosing between speed and texture.

Of course, microwave and air fryer combinations aren’t entirely new. Brands such as Smeg have already explored the concept, while plenty of modern microwaves come with a range of additional cooking functions.

What makes the Ninja Crispi Microwave particularly interesting, however, is its FusionCrisp technology, which is designed to bring both cooking methods together rather than simply offering two separate functions. It comes with a 5.5-quart glass cooking dish and a nonstick crisper plate, which sits on top when you want to air fry and crisp up your food.

Another part that makes it stand out is that there isn’t a rotating plate inside, opening up a lot more space to cook more dishes at once.

It’s not just about reheating leftovers. For example, if you want to make a pasta bake, the microwave can cook the pasta, while the air fryer crisps up the cheese on top.

There’s one thing to consider before buying it, though. Measuring 20.3 x 17.56 x 14.1 inches, the microwave is hardly compact. It takes up a fair amount of counter space, so while it could free up room if you’re replacing a separate microwave and air fryer, it’s not necessarily the ideal solution for a small apartment kitchen.

Then there’s the $449.99 price tag. That’s a considerable amount to spend on a microwave, particularly when a basic model can handle everyday reheating for a fraction of the cost. But if you’re someone who regularly reaches for both a microwave and an air fryer, the combination could make a lot more sense.

articles.title: Vivo’s first Pro Max phone proves its Ultra is still in a league of its own
articles.summary: The Vivo X500 Pro Max is a great flagship phone, but a step back from my favorite phone camera.
articles.body: When I declared this spring that Vivo’s X300 Ultra had the best cameras in any phone, two things made it stand out in my mind: its excellent main camera with a narrow 35mm focal length and what remains the most capable ultrawide in any phone worldwide. You won’t find either in the new X500 Pro Max. It has an impressive camera system with world-leading dynamic range and the same great telephoto lens found in the Ultra. But it’s lost a little something of what made its predecessor quite so special. [Product: Vivo X500 Pro Max | The X500 Pro Max is the latest in a trend that’s seen China’s major Android players roll out Pro Max models, including Xiaomi, Oppo, Honor, and now Vivo. The new models close the gap between their previous Pro flagships and camera-centric Ultra models — or, if you prefer to be cynical about it, are an excuse to slap “Max” on the box to better mask RAM-induced price hikes. A little of column A, a little of column B, I suspect. The Pro Max adopts plenty of flagship features found in the older Ultra. It’s the same size, for one, and has a matching 1440p, 144Hz OLED display. It’s got an even bigger battery — 7,800mAh — which breezes through two days of use, with similar 90W wired and 40W wireless charging. Unlike the Ultra it doesn’t use the latest Snapdragon chipset, but its MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro delivers roughly comparable performance. It even features the exact same periscope telephoto camera, one of the best in any phone. Then there’s the price: €1,799 (about $2,000) puts this squarely in the ultra-premium bracket. But despite all that, this isn’t a true successor to the X300 Ultra, which is still rumored to see a direct sequel sometime next year. The X500 Pro Max still sits half a step down in Vivo’s hierarchy, and so it would be a little unfair to expect it to match or beat the older Ultra. The problem isn’t that this camera is worse than that phone’s, though, but that it’s much less unique. [Image: [Image: As you’d expect from a step-down model, the 50-megapixel, 1/1.28-inch-type main camera sensor is both smaller and lower resolution than the Ultra’s, impacting its quality. But the newer phone offsets that a little thanks to one edge on the Ultra: It uses Sony’s new Lytia L910 image sensor, which features LOFIC technology that enables a wider 17-stop dynamic range, with the enhancements primarily in the highlights. But the X300 Ultra’s camera wasn’t only notable for technical quality. I loved the fact that it adopted a 35mm focal length, and am disappointed that the Pro Max returns to the same 24mm focal length found on iPhones and countless others. This, like most phones’ main cameras, is a wide-angle in truth. It’s designed to take in as much of a scene as possible, reserving the ultrawide for truly large landscape shots. It’s part of why I’ve taken to stepping back and using the telephoto by default on many phones, enjoying the tighter framing and better bokeh, but that often brings other quality compromises, especially in lower light. A 35mm main camera, by contrast, feels closer to many of the kit and prime lenses you might grab for a regular camera, narrow enough to use for portraits and purposeful framing. It sits more evenly in between the 14mm ultrawide and 85mm telephoto, giving you natural options across the range. You could of course just use the X500 Pro Max’s 24mm main camera and zoom in a little, but then you’re wasting some of the sensor and relying on digital zoom tricks, rather than making the most of the lens’s optics. I’m stubborn about shooting with my cameras’ full focal lengths whenever I can, and you should be too. [Image: The design has a clever trick to mask the depth of the camera island: The body itself slopes up to meet it. If there’s a saving grace to the decision to return to a wider main camera, it’s that it helps make up for the X500 Pro Max’s other shortcoming: a much smaller ultrawide camera sensor. The ethos of the X300 Ultra was that all three lenses should deliver comparable quality. As such, it treated its ultrawide like another main camera, with a large sensor and even optical image stabilization, a rarity on wide lenses. In fact, its sensor is the same size as the X500 Pro Max’s main camera, so a repeat of that feat was never especially likely, but the 1/2.75-inch-type ultrawide in the X500 Pro Max is still a notable step down. Taking the phone to a nighttime Champions League game, there was a clear gap in quality moving from the ultrawide to the other two lenses. Under the bright stadium lights, the ultrawide blew out the white details on the pitch and player kits and left the crowd in comparative darkness. The main and ultrawide were able to bring more detail out of the dimly lit spectators and better handle the highlights on the pitch, without entirely giving up on the contrast that gave the scene its character. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: It’s important to put these gripes in context: This is a truly excellent camera system for a phone, and still more capable than any you can officially buy in the US. The returning telephoto in particular is exceptional; every lens benefits from Vivo’s naturalistic color-tuning, developed together with Zeiss, and video capabilities include Log recording and 4K at 240fps slow motion. It supports Vivo’s teleconverter lenses too, including a seriously chunky 400mm option. It’s just a shame that the most interesting elements of the Ultra’s camera haven’t trickled down to its first Pro Max too. Strangely, another phone I’ve tested this month feels like it picked up where the X300 Ultra left off: Oppo’s Find X10 Pro Max, a pretty direct rival to this phone. Its triple 200-megapixel camera system still uses a wide-angle main camera, but at least includes a substantially improved ultrawide camera to create that same feeling that each of its three rear lenses is of comparable quality. All I hope now is that when the X500 Ultra rolls around come spring, it builds on the success of the older Ultra, and perhaps finds new ways to make its cameras stand out. After all, if the Pro Max costs €1,799, the Ultra could cost substantially more — and will have its work cut out to prove it’s worth it. Photography by Dominic Preston / The Verge

articles.title: Dollyy Javved on cosmetic enhancements and beauty standards: There’s no shame in accepting it
articles.summary: While celebrities often shy away from admitting to cosmetic procedures, Dollyy Javved, who has been part of shows such as Chhoriyan Chali Gaon and
articles.body: While celebrities often shy away from admitting to cosmetic procedures, Dollyy Javved, who has been part of shows such as Chhoriyan Chali Gaon and Alliance, is candid about her experiences with enhancements, including chin fillers and Botox. She believes there should be greater openness around cosmetic procedures, particularly because public appearances can create unrealistic expectations about natural looks. According to her, being honest about such choices can help people understand that appearance is sometimes the result of treatments and enhancements rather than simply genetics. She says, “What is there to hide? Getting fillers and undergoing cosmetic procedures is normal. It is important for people to know that a lot goes into looking a certain way and that not everything is natural. Some people choose not to disclose their cosmetic enhancements for fear of being trolled, which is why greater acceptance of such choices is necessary. I am open about it because I do not care about trolls. I have always been authentic and do not shy away from discussing these things because I see no shame in them.”Growing up, Dollyy was often told that the scar on her forehead affected her appearance, but she has never viewed it as a flaw. She believes that comments about physical features can influence how people see themselves, particularly during their formative years, when they are still developing confidence and learning to accept their appearance. For her, self-acceptance is not something that happens overnight; it takes time and the ability to look beyond other people's opinions. She recounts, “Since childhood, people have told me that the scar on my forehead is not pretty and that I should get it removed. Personally, I have never seen it as a flaw. Learning to love yourself is a long journey. When you become a teenager, you start nitpicking your flaws, sometimes because others point them out. It is important to tune out such comments and for people to be more compassionate towards others.”On experimenting with fillers and choosing what suits her:Her experience with cosmetic enhancements has also been about discovering what works for her rather than following a particular beauty ideal. She has tried different procedures, but that does not mean she intends to retain every enhancement. Her decision to dissolve her chin fillers, for instance, came after she realised that she preferred her natural facial shape. She also credits her sister, Uorfi, for encouraging her to consider lip fillers, something she had been contemplating for a while. Explaining how she arrived at these choices, Dollyy says, “I had always wanted to try lip fillers because I used to overline my lips excessively, to the point where they looked bad. My sister, Uorfi, suggested fillers, so I decided to try them. I got lip fillers about a year ago and also had Botox injected into my masseter muscles. When I got my lip fillers done, the doctor suggested adding a little chin filler for symmetry. However, after a year, I realised I was happy with my round face, so I got the fillers dissolved.”Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Join us for the 2026-27 Wisconsin basketball season on the SB Nation app
articles.summary: Our new game chats are perfect for the return of college hoops.
articles.body:
Almost two months ago, we announced the release of our new app, which you can find here or by searching SB Nation in your neighborhood app store. The app is available in North America, and we're working on Europe and the rest of the world as we speak!

Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past seven weeks and have been using it, but if you are a big college basketball fan, it's also entirely possible a few of you missed it!

The goal with this app was to make it easier to join the community, and specifically comment, read the comments, and make your own posts, as well as keeping all the community posts – articles on the front page, Feed posts from you – front and center.

One of the most exciting new features is the game chat, which some of you may have already test-driven during the preseason. It makes it easier to follow along with the barrage of comments that come during games, and gets to the heart of why so many of you spend time in our community. Faster loading comments and notifications when someone replies to your comments and Feed posts are creating a more fun experience that you're not going to find anywhere else.

We also wanted to elevate the community's contributions by putting your Feed posts inside one stream alongside all the other articles from the site. To that end, more people have seen your posts and more people have commented on them. In fact, we've set single-day commenting records three different times in the last several weeks.

And if you prefer just reading our traditional front page articles, there's an option at the top to do that.

So, thanks for making us part of your routine. If you haven't checked it out, you can get the app for iOS or Android . And if you're not an app user, that's OK! We're glad to have you following along in whatever way makes you most comfortable.
